subject: Bridge signal spike — deep-dive, action grid, and customer comms
messages:
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: [Alert] Bridge latency spike affecting TrailSend endpoints

Markus / team—

Monitoring caught a sustained spike on the "bridge" queue beginning 08:50 PDT. Quick summary:
- QPS on bridge-service for region us-west rose ~3.2x baseline for ~22 minutes.
- p95 increased from 140ms -> 1.1s; p99 touched 2.4s.
- KV-cache eviction rate increased sharply (see attached kv_eviction_excerpt.log).
- TrailSend endpoints (/v1/generate and /v1/realtime) showed 7% 5xx and elevated tail latency for a subset of requests.

Immediate triage steps taken:
- Reduced concurrency on a handful of suspect instances to limit queue depth.
- Rolled a temporary routing rule to divert non-critical traffic to a lower-latency model variant.

Needs and asks:
1) Karthik: can you run a quick queue-depth vs kernel-scheduling correlation and confirm whether the spike is evict-driven or scheduling-driven?
2) Product (Marissa): do we approve the canary fallback to the quantized model for TrailSend for the next 4 hours if it reduces tail latency?
3) CS (Neha): we should prep a short customer note acknowledging impact and ETA.

Attachments: qps_spike_20260522.png (metric snapshot), kv_eviction_excerpt.log (tail).

Ben
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Alert] Bridge latency spike affecting TrailSend endpoints

On Fri, May 22, 2026 at 09:12 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Monitoring caught a sustained spike on the "bridge" queue beginning 08:50 PDT.
>
> Immediate triage steps taken: reduced concurrency; temporary routing rule.

I'll take the kernel/queue analysis. Initial hypotheses:
- We are seeing KV-cache churn on hot keys coming from TrailSend's heavy fanout (batch size distribution skewed). When the KV set is evicted, we pay warm-start costs that amplify tail latency under load.
- Scheduling preemption due to a single noisy instance also possible.

Planned checks (ETA 45m):
- Correlate per-instance KV hit-rate with p95 windows.
- Confirm if the routing change reduced tail metrics for the affected endpoints.
- Run a targeted hot-key profiling on a small sample.

Short-term mitigation suggestions (approval required):
- Canary fallback to a quantized-compatible variant for TrailSend's production route (expected p95 reduction ~30-40%, potential small quality delta).
- If acceptable, set an automated revert after 4 hours and capture eval prompts.

Marissa: if you greenlight, I'll coordinate the rollout.
Karthik
Principal Engineer, Runtime
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bridge latency spike — deep-dive, action grid, and customer comms

Thanks for the quick triage. Approving a controlled canary fallback under these constraints:
- Scope: TrailSend production route only, <= 20% of requests initially, auto-scale to 100% if stability improves and we see no unacceptable regressions.
- Duration: 4 hour canary window with automatic rollback on error rate > 2% above baseline.
- Data capture: force a small eval set from TrailSend's prompts (CS to coordinate consent).

Action grid (owners / ETA):
- Karthik: kernel/queue correlation + hot-key profile (45m).
- Ben: implement canary routing rule and rollback monitors (30m).
- Neha: prep the customer-facing note draft and list of prompts for eval (60m).
- Grace: schedule a 30-min sync with TrailSend if they want a live update (ASAP).
- Markus: coordinate executive note if this expands.

Marissa
Head of Product, Inference Platform
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: elena@trailsend.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: TrailSend update: short-term mitigation and next steps

Elena / TrailSend ops—

I'm Neha from Redwood's CS team. We saw an elevated error rate and tail latency impacting some of your requests earlier this morning (08:50–09:12 PDT). We're deploying a controlled routing fallback for your production route to reduce tail latency while we complete a deeper engineering analysis.

What we are doing now:
- Canary fallback to a quantized-compatible model for a small percentage of your traffic (20% initial).
- 4-hour monitoring window with automatic rollback triggers on errors.
- Collecting a de-identified eval set (with your consent) to check for any regressions in quality.

ETA and ask:
- Expected visible improvement within 10–20 minutes from now.
- Could you confirm whether we have your consent to sample up to 500 de-identified prompts for validation?

We apologize for the disruption. Markus is looped in for product and exec updates.

—Neha
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: elena@trailsend.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 11:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TrailSend update: short-term mitigation and next steps

Hi Neha—

Thanks for the update and for the quick rollback plan. We are seeing intermittent timeouts that are affecting checkout latency. Please proceed with the sampling; we approve the de-identified 500-prompt set.

A couple of asks from our side:
- Can you confirm whether the fallback will change any tokenization or hallucination risk? We can't accept a meaningful drop in result quality for ML-complete flows.
- If you end up rolling back to heavier throttling, we need an ETA for a full mitigation.

If helpful, we can jump on a quick call in 30 minutes.

—Elena Ruiz
Head of Ops, TrailSend
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: elena@trailsend.com
Date: Sat, 23 May 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-mortem note and roadmap asks (actioned)

Team—

Wrap-up and decisions:
- Mitigation: Canary fallback to the quantized variant reduced p95 for TrailSend from ~1.1s -> ~260ms within 12 minutes of the rollout. Error rate returned to baseline.
- Root cause (prelim): hot-key driven KV eviction plus queue amplification under a microburst of fanout requests. No single kernel scheduling bug confirmed; follow-up kernel tracing scheduled.

Immediate follow-ups (owners):
- Karthik: file tracing artifact and root-cause doc (RFC linked above) — due EOD Mon.
- Ben: add a short-lived adaptive-batching knob to the bridge runtime for extreme fanout (prototype flag) — due Wed.
- Marissa: prioritize a roadmap ticket for persistent KV and hot-key mitigation (RFC/priority to be discussed in next PLG sync).
- Neha: send final customer brief to TrailSend with a short timeline for permanent mitigations.

Customer note sent (Elena cc'd). We will log the incident as INC-TS-3421 and attach metrics and artifacts to the HubSpot record (HubSpot: 20933).

Thanks for the rapid cross-functional response. This is a clear product -> infra roadmap signal: persistent KV and adaptive batching should be elevated. Linking to the follow-up RFC here: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/216-adaptive-batching

Markus Klein
Director, Site Reliability & Field Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: customer_update_draft.docx
